OWNER-REVIEW DRAFT
Privacy notice

Plain-language summary of how this frontend enquiry experience handles your information.

Draft for owner review—not legal advice. This notice should be reviewed before public launch.

Information you enter

The ride planner asks for journey details, your name, phone number, optional email address, and optional instructions. Do not enter identity documents, payment details, or other unnecessary sensitive information.

What stays in your browser

Your planner entries are held in page memory so they remain available while you move around the site. This implementation does not send them to a PINS Cabs server or database and does not intentionally store personal contact details in local storage.

Location search and maps

Searching sends the place or address you enter to the configured search service (Photon by default, using OpenStreetMap data). Using your current location requires browser permission. GPS coordinates and points selected on the map are sent to the address lookup service (OpenStreetMap Nominatim by default) to find an address. Map tiles are requested from OpenStreetMap; these providers also receive technical information such as your IP address. Recent locations and search results are kept in memory for this browser session. The prepared WhatsApp enquiry includes the pickup and destination coordinates and map links.

What happens when you continue

When you select “Continue to WhatsApp,” the site prepares a message and opens WhatsApp through a user-initiated link. Nothing is sent automatically. Information is then handled under WhatsApp’s terms and the communication practices of PINS Cabs.

Calling and maps

Telephone and Google Maps links open external applications or services. Those providers may process technical information under their own privacy terms.

Booking status

A prepared or sent enquiry is not a confirmed booking. PINS Cabs confirms availability and final pricing separately.

Privacy notice

Plain-language summary of how this frontend enquiry experience handles your information.

Draft for owner review—not legal advice. This notice should be reviewed before public launch.

Information you enter

The ride planner asks for journey details, your name, phone number, optional email address, and optional instructions. Do not enter identity documents, payment details, or other unnecessary sensitive information.

What stays in your browser

Your planner entries are held in page memory so they remain available while you move around the site. This implementation does not send them to a PINS Cabs server or database and does not intentionally store personal contact details in local storage.

Location search and maps

Searching sends the place or address you enter to the configured search service (Photon by default, using OpenStreetMap data). Using your current location requires browser permission. GPS coordinates and points selected on the map are sent to the address lookup service (OpenStreetMap Nominatim by default) to find an address. Map tiles are requested from OpenStreetMap; these providers also receive technical information such as your IP address. Recent locations and search results are kept in memory for this browser session. The prepared WhatsApp enquiry includes the pickup and destination coordinates and map links.

What happens when you continue

When you select “Continue to WhatsApp,” the site prepares a message and opens WhatsApp through a user-initiated link. Nothing is sent automatically. Information is then handled under WhatsApp’s terms and the communication practices of PINS Cabs.

Calling and maps

Telephone and Google Maps links open external applications or services. Those providers may process technical information under their own privacy terms.

Booking status

A prepared or sent enquiry is not a confirmed booking. PINS Cabs confirms availability and final pricing separately.

What to include in an airport transfer enquiry

Prepare flight, pickup and luggage details before requesting an airport transfer with PINS Cabs.

Start with the flight

Share the flight number, travel date and whether you need an arrival pickup or departure drop-off. For an arrival, discuss a pickup time that allows for completing airport formalities. For a departure, check your airline's arrival guidance and agree a suitable collection time. Do not assume a fixed journey duration.

Describe the people and bags

Count everyone who needs a passenger seat. List large suitcases separately from small bags and mention strollers or other bulky items. The listed seat count is not a luggage guarantee: a fully occupied vehicle can have less storage available. Ask for the actual layout to be confirmed.

Agree where to meet

For an airport pickup, confirm the meeting point and the phone number you will use after landing. For a hotel or home collection, use an accurate map pin and identify the entrance. Add any access instructions that would help the driver find you.

Check the quote and changes

Ask whether waiting, parking and other journey charges are included. If the flight or passenger count changes, contact the team to agree a revised arrangement. Keep the confirmed pickup details available during travel; submitting the online planner alone is not a confirmed reservation.

Choosing a vehicle for your passenger count and luggage

Count passengers first

Enter the number of guests excluding the driver. The planner suggests cars and compact vans for parties of up to four, larger vans for five to fourteen, and buses above fourteen. It excludes any class with fewer listed seats than your passenger count. Bus hire and goods transport have their own service filters.

Compare van and bus classes

Treat luggage as a separate requirement

Provide both a bag count and a description of large items. Seating capacity alone does not tell you whether suitcases or equipment will fit. For an airport group, ask the team to confirm passenger and luggage space together before choosing the final vehicle.

Confirm comfort and access

The Non-AC Van is explicitly non-air-conditioned. For other classes, discuss the features of the actual available vehicle, not just its illustrative photograph.
